headline_marked: Egypt coach claims [[side was 'cheated' out of World Cup quarter-finals]] after 3-2 loss to Argentina
headline: Egypt coach claims side was 'cheated' out of World Cup quarter-finals after 3-2 loss to Argentina
summary: Hossam Hassan fumed over VAR decisions and scheduling, suggesting officials wanted to keep Lionel Messi and the world champions in the competition.
details: Argentina staged a stunning late comeback from 2-0 down to defeat Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday, knocking the Pharaohs out of the World Cup.
Egypt coach Hossam Hassan exploded in a post-match press conference, claiming his side had been 'cheated unfairly' and suffered 'injustice' during the match.
The controversy centers on a Mostafa Zico goal that was ruled out by VAR for a foul on Lisandro Martinez, and a denied penalty for a pull on Hamdy Fathy.
Argentina fought back with goals from Cristian Romero and Lionel Messi, before Enzo Fernandez scored the winner. Messi's eighth goal of the tournament secured the equalizer.
Hassan speculated that officials were under pressure to ensure the world champions and Lionel Messi remained in the tournament, citing a lack of 'respect or fair play'.
The coach also criticized the 12pm kick-off time, arguing that such scheduling is unsuitable for professional football and questioning the decisions made off the pitch.
caption:
“We have been cheated unfairly today.” Egypt's coach is fuming after a dramatic 3-2 loss to Argentina.

Argentina staged a stunning late comeback from 2-0 down to defeat Egypt 3-2 on Tuesday, knocking the Pharaohs out of the World Cup.

Egypt coach Hossam Hassan exploded in a post-match press conference, claiming his side had been 'cheated unfairly' and suffered 'injustice' during the match.

The controversy centers on a Mostafa Zico goal that was ruled out by VAR for a foul on Lisandro Martinez, and a denied penalty for a pull on Hamdy Fathy.

Argentina fought back with goals from Cristian Romero and Lionel Messi, before Enzo Fernandez scored the winner. Messi's eighth goal of the tournament secured the equalizer.

Hassan speculated that officials were under pressure to ensure the world champions and Lionel Messi remained in the tournament, citing a lack of 'respect or fair play'.

The coach also criticized the 12pm kick-off time, arguing that such scheduling is unsuitable for professional football and questioning the decisions made off the pitch.

headline_marked: Iran's [[Khamenei's body arrives in Iraq]] for funeral processions
headline: Iran's Khamenei's body arrives in Iraq for funeral processions
summary: The remains of the late supreme leader arrived at Najaf International Airport ahead of services in the country's holy cities.
details: The body of Iran's supreme leader Ali Khamenei arrived at Najaf International Airport in Iraq on Tuesday night, according to Iraqi state media.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and senior Iraqi officials, including Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, were present to receive the remains.
The arrival took place via a Mahan Air flight, as reported by Iraqi state TV.
The body will be taken to Iraq's holy cities, which are home to shrines most revered by Shia Muslims, for funeral processions.
Ali Khamenei was killed on the first day of the Middle East war.
caption:
The body of Iran's supreme leader Ali Khamenei has arrived in Iraq.

The body of Iran's supreme leader Ali Khamenei arrived at Najaf International Airport in Iraq on Tuesday night, according to Iraqi state media.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and senior Iraqi officials, including Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi, were present to receive the remains.

The arrival took place via a Mahan Air flight, as reported by Iraqi state TV.

The body will be taken to Iraq's holy cities, which are home to shrines most revered by Shia Muslims, for funeral processions.

Ali Khamenei was killed on the first day of the Middle East war.
